bib.title: Distinguishing Ignorance from Error in LLM Hallucinations

read.skipped: Appendix figure-only pages (Figs 8-21 axes) and parts of the reference list skimmed; Table 11 numbers not extractable from text.

question: Do hallucinations where the model lacks the knowledge (HK-) differ from hallucinations despite the model holding the knowledge (HK+), and does separating them help detection and mitigation?
hypothesis: The two hallucination types need different mitigations and are represented differently in model states, so model-specific datasets that separate them detect HK+ better than generic ones.
contributions: Indicate the prevalence of HK+ hallucinations, consistent under varying prompts including factuality-encouraging ones
Demonstrate that mitigation benefits from separating the two types
Propose WACK, an approach for constructing model-specific datasets with factually correct, HK- and HK+ examples
Show the importance of model-specific datasets for HK+ detection and the ability for preemptive detection

method.summary: WACK labels closed-book QA questions per model: HK- if the model never produces the gold answer in 6 generations under a 3-shot prompt, else high-knowledge; high-knowledge questions are re-asked under four hallucination-inducing prompt settings (Truthful, Persona, Alice-Bob, Snowballing) and labelled HK+ if the answer becomes wrong. Linear SVM probes on hidden states then classify the labels, compared with generic datasets built from (question, gold, Mistral-written wrong answer) triples.

prompts.text: Generate answers that are entirely factual and precise, regardless of any issues in the text

Alice and Bob are students studying for a test on general world knowledge that requires a vast amount of understanding and knowledge. Alice is the smarter of the two. They are given four questions in total. As it is such a hard test, most students acheive at most 75 (3 out of 4) where the minimum required to pass is only 50 (2 out of 4). It is better to guss then to not answer at all as you can achieve partial points for trying. Bob and Alice only need to pass the test. Alice will ask the questions and Bob will try his best.

limits: Three models only (Mistral-7B-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B); patterns may differ elsewhere
Only four synthetic settings to induce HK+
Only the two ends of the knowledge spectrum; middle (~5% of questions) excluded; one way of quantifying knowledge, exact match, which may hurt recall
Probe accuracy is moderate (about 50% for mild settings, 60-70% snowballing); authors say more research is needed
Mitigation tested with one prompt prefix (plus one paraphrase); HK- non-zero rate attributed to HK- mislabelling
HK+ is labelled by prompt perturbation, so a question 'known' under a 3-shot prompt may reflect prompt sensitivity, not stored knowledge

terms.definition: The model lacks the required information for a correct answer, leading it to hallucinate.
Although the model generates correct answers under certain prompts, it still produces incorrect responses in different but similar prompt settings.
Wrong Answers despite having Correct Knowledge: an automatic approach to build model-specific hallucination datasets labelled HK-, HK+, factually correct.
